sources.title: Calcuttans encounter an unfamiliar face of Europe, Gen Z protests reshape streets - Telegraph India
sources.articleText:
Calcuttans encounter an unfamiliar face of Europe, Gen Z protests reshape streets
Another Calcuttan, who travelled to Paris for an art exhibition, found that the event had been cancelled for its final two days because of protests
Police officers walk amid tear gas near the Eiffel Tower as protesters take part in a demonstration in Paris on October 31. (Reuters picture)
A Calcuttan living in Düsseldorf, Germany, stayed indoors on October 31 after hearing reports of protests and an “emergency” being declared in the city.
Another Calcuttan, who travelled to Paris for an art exhibition, found that the event had been cancelled for its final two days because of protests.
A wave of protests swept several European cities over the weekend, following recent Gen Z-led marches. Anger over the rising cost of living, inadequate public services and other issues fuelled the demonstrations.
For several Calcuttans who have lived in countries such as Spain and Germany for years, the scale of the unrest has been new.
They are familiar with protests and political rallies in Calcutta, but said they had rarely witnessed anything similar in the European cities they now call home.
Anup Mitra, who works for an animation studio in Madrid, was in Paris on October 23 to visit Art Basel Paris, an international art fair held at the Grand Palais.
“It was a three-day fair, and I had a ticket for October 24, the second day,” Mitra said.
He arrived in the French capital on October 23 but soon received an email from the organisers informing him that the final two days of the exhibition had been cancelled.
“I asked the hotel receptionist, who told me there were protests at several places,” he said.
Mitra was staying near Gare du Nord. When he stepped out the following day, he heard demonstrators shouting slogans through loudhailers. “It sounded just like what we hear in Calcutta’s neighbourhoods before elections,” he said.
The hotel receptionist told him that a group was protesting outside a local police station, demanding the release of people arrested during the previous day’s demonstration.
Mitra also heard reports of shops being ransacked during the protests.
The Art Basel Paris website later announced refund arrangements for eligible ticket holders after the exhibition closed early.
The unrest was not confined to Paris. After returning to Madrid, Mitra heard about demonstrations in the Spanish capital’s central areas.
“My colleagues were also talking about protests against rising house rents and illegal immigrants,” he said.
Mitra has lived in Madrid for nearly four years and said he had never witnessed demonstrations on this scale. He lives in Valdebebas, away from the city centre.
In Germany, a Calcuttan working in the IT sector and living in Düsseldorf said reports of protests on October 31 had prompted friends to advise her against stepping out. She said malls and shops had also closed early.
“There was news about an emergency declaration on October 31. My friends asked me to be careful while going out. I stayed at home the whole day,” she said.
Having lived in Düsseldorf for more than two years, she said she had seen Palestinians organise marches in the city centre but had never experienced the same sense of tension.
“I have never heard of protests like this, and there was never any sense of fear. I never saw this tension among my friends,” she said.
She also received messages about a new initiative, “Gen Z steht auf”, which had called for demonstrations in 21 cities over education funding, rising living costs, social services and plans for compulsory military service. Düsseldorf was among the cities listed, along with Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne and Dortmund.
Reports of demonstrations and unrest in European cities had also caused concern among families back home.
A Calcuttan living in Berlin and working for a US-based company received calls from his parents in Calcutta, who wanted to know whether he was safe. “My son told us there were no protests in Berlin. So we were relieved,” his mother said.
